title: Drone incursions over bases, 2023-2026
notes: A stable small community in the 24 September run (stability 0.89): the base incursions and the February 2023 shootdowns.

lead.text: Since December 2023 unidentified drones have repeatedly flown over US military bases, from weeks of incursions over the F-22 base at Langley to a reported drone over Barksdale Air Force Base in March 2026, and the NORAD commander said in October 2024 that he knew of no foreign nexus for Langley. Langley produced no attribution and no public explanation; what followed was a counter-drone task force and wider authority for base commanders.

summary.text: The Air Force confirmed that Langley first observed drone activity on the evening of 6 December 2023 and had multiple incursions through the month; the response included F-16 patrols with aerial refuelling, NASA WB-57F surveillance orbits, FBI coordination through NORTHCOM and FAA notification.

A year later a wave of sightings over New Jersey and neighbouring states produced more than 5,000 reports to the FBI, and on 17 December 2024 DoD, DHS, the FBI and the FAA said jointly that they had identified nothing anomalous.
On 9 March 2026 Barksdale Air Force Base reported a drone over the installation, raised force protection to FPCON Charlie and ordered personnel to shelter in place.

The institutional answer was Joint Interagency Task Force 401, set up in August 2025 under Brig. Gen. Matt Ross, a DoD Inspector General evaluation of ten affected installations, and January 2026 guidance widening commanders' authority to act.

The topic also takes in the February 2023 shootdowns, when NORAD-controlled fighters destroyed three unidentified objects in four days, and the FY2026 NDAA's demand for a history of NORAD and Northern Command UAP intercepts back to 2004.

record.text: The New Jersey statement says officials followed up about 100 specific leads and found commercial, hobbyist and law enforcement drones, manned aircraft, helicopters and stars mistaken for drones. The same assessment acknowledged limited recent sightings over military facilities in restricted airspace, contradicting earlier White House denials.

Wright-Patterson Air Force Base closed its airspace for nearly four hours on 14 and 15 December 2024 because of unauthorised drone activity, days before the federal statement that nothing anomalous had been found.
Barksdale's chief of public affairs confirmed on 9 March 2026 that the base had received a report of an unmanned aerial system operating over the installation.

The Inspector General's report DODIG-2026-045 of 21 January 2026 evaluated ten installations that had experienced incursions, interviewed officials from 31 DoD components and four federal agencies, and found inconsistent policies and approval processes that delayed counter-drone deployment.
Guidance announced on 30 January 2026 removed the fence-line limitation, defined unauthorised surveillance as an explicit threat and gave commanders discretion based on the totality of circumstances.

A Secret Privy Council memo of 14 February 2023 to Prime Minister Trudeau records that exploitation of the object the US engaged on 10 February had not been completed, and that the Yukon object remained unverified as to function, propulsion or affiliation to any nation-state.

The Lake Huron object was destroyed on 12 February 2023 by two F-16s of the Minnesota Air National Guard with an AIM-9X at about 20,000 feet. Infrared video of the engagement was released through PURSUE on 22 May 2026, with the entry noting a lack of substantiated chain of custody.
NORAD kept issuing intercept press releases through 2026, including several for temporary flight restriction violations in the Northeast and over New Jersey.

Section 1671 of the FY2026 NDAA, enacted 18 December 2025, requires briefings on UAP intercepts by NORAD and Northern Command, the first covering intercepts not previously reported since 1 January 2004.

The pattern has a documented precedent: NORAD's commander-in-chief reported on 11 November 1975 that reliable military personnel at Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot and Falconbridge had visually sighted suspicious objects.

claimed.text: Gen. Mark Kelly told the Wall Street Journal that at least one Langley drone was about 20 feet long, flying at more than 100 mph at 3,000 to 4,000 feet. A Langley spokesperson said none of the incursions appeared hostile but that anything in restricted airspace threatens flight safety.

NORAD commander Gen. Gregory Guillot said in October 2024 that he could say only roughly the number and altitude of the Langley drones and knew of no organised or unorganised foreign nexus. He made Langley the centrepiece of his counter-drone assessment on taking command, and NORAD counted more than 600 drone reports over US installations since 2022.

Guillot said in March 2026 that detections over military installations had increased from the year before and that about a quarter of detected drones were now defeated, against almost none previously. Restricted-airspace sightings were reported to have risen 26 percent in 2025.

Reporting describes waves of 12 to 15 drones over Barksdale's flight line with non-commercial signal characteristics and resistance to jamming, following the launch of the bombing campaign against Iran, with a single counter-drone kit fielded; a NORTHCOM spokesman declined to name the affected bases.
A pilot over Lake Huron is heard saying he could not tell from the targeting pod whether the object was metallic but could see lines coming down below it.
Protective netting to shield Langley's F-22s was reported to be under consideration by October 2024, and Guillot set up the Falcon Peak counter-drone demonstrations.

contested.text: The four agencies attributed New Jersey to hobbyists and misidentification on about 100 leads, while Langley was never publicly explained; the board reads the creation of a standing task force under a general officer as refuting the hobbyist explanation.

Sean Kirkpatrick said of the February 2023 shootdowns that the objects were balloons, while the Canadian government's own Secret memo recorded the Yukon object as unverified as to function and propulsion.

On the board's reading, AARO's published case work and its FY2025 report do not assess the Langley, New Jersey or Barksdale incursions, which are handled as force protection by NORTHCOM and JIATF-401; this rests on absence, not on any stated ruling.

questions: Who operated the drones over Langley and Barksdale, and has any government body attributed them?
What do the classified annexes of Guillot's counter-drone assessment say, and how many incursions did NORAD count at each installation in 2025 and 2026?
Which ten installations did the Inspector General evaluate, and what does the redacted part of DODIG-2026-045 contain?
Under what directive, funding line and reporting chain does JIATF-401 operate?
Was the exploitation of the object shot down over Alaska on 10 February 2023 ever completed, and what did it find?
What has the section 1671 briefing on NORAD intercepts since 2004 told Congress?
